/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

Fix: tighten `recoverableZeroRed` to require a DECIDED head — `tally.real >= 1` (at least one real concluded check) plus red === 0. Update the pure-module tests first (TDD: adjust the expectation for the empty-rollup case), then the smAgent rung picks it up automatically since it calls the same function... wait, does my rung call `recoverableZeroRed`? No — the rung inlines `gTallyVf.red === 0 && probeHeadVerdictVf() !== 'failure'`. I should switch the rung to use the module's function for a single source of truth.

Wait, also the rung checks `probeHeadVerdictVf() !== 'failure'` (the dispatched verdict). Keep that in the rung; use the module for the tally bar.

TDD order: update module test first (empty rollup → recoverableZeroRed false, stub-only → false, real-pending → true still, red → false, null → false). Then change the module. Then run module tests. Then run smAgent tests.

But hold on — is `real >= 1` the right discriminator vs the sticky tests? Sticky pr-206: `github_get_commit_check_runs` mock returns `{check_runs: []}` → real 0 → hold ✓. My AC2: quality success (real) + merge/11 (bokeping) → real 1 → clear ✓. Also the in-flight REAL check case: quality IN_PROGRESS → pending 1, real 1 → recoverableZeroRed true → clear while a run is in flight — that's the 'the verdict owns it' stance: when the run concludes red, the re-park ladder catches it. OK.

Edge: what about a head with ONLY stub checks (merge-bot skipped)? real 0 → hold ✓ (can't distinguish dissolved-red from never-validated).

Now also the smAgent rung comment should be updated to describe the decided-head bar. Let me implement:

1. Update test_guestValidationPath.js recoverableZeroRed tests: add empty rollup → false, stub-only → false. Change the doc.
2. Update module: `return !!tally && tally.red === 0 && tally.real >= 1;` + header doc line.
3. smAgent rung: replace inline `gTallyVf.red === 0` with `guestValidationPathModule.recoverableZeroRed(gTallyVf)` — keeps single source. The `guestRungWhyVf` message mentions counts — keep using gTallyVf.real.

Check the empty-rollup test at line 39: `realCheckTally([])` — what does the module test assert for realCheckTally? It asserts tally fields; fine.

Let me view the module test lines 39-60 and the recoverable test again (lines 145-160 above).

The fa#923 sticky-park conflict is clear: my guest self-clear fires on a **zero-check head** (`real === 0`), which is exactly the "parked before any checks ran" shape fa#923 protects. The discriminator: the punished head must be **decided** (≥1 real concluded check) before "no red" means "the red dissolved". TDD — fix the module tests first:

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

arguments.content:
## What changed
Closes the guest-PR validation dead zone (live IstiN/flutter_agent_harness #1634/#1615/#1591: fork PRs sat `pr_approved` + CLEAN for hours with a manual `ai_validating` label — no merge, no validation). Adds a `merge-validated-guest` lane (deployed `sm_github.json`, ordered directly below `merge-validated`): human-authored (`notMachine`) armed+approved CLEAN guests whose rollup carries no concluded verdict may merge when the head's real check-run census is zero-failing and the `ai_validating` event was labeled by a non-machine actor.

## Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/guestValidationPath.js` (`realCheckTally`, `mergeableZeroFailing`, `recoverableZeroRed`, `isManualArm`, `newestArmEvent`, dead-zone carry) — all policy decisions unit-tested in isolation, loaded real by the smAgent tests.
- Merge gate `guestZeroFailingMergeGate` (rule flag `guestZeroFailing`) is fail-closed on every probe: real red, real in-flight check, any active head workflow run, missing/unreadable arm event, or probe error → refuse; bookkeeping stubs (`merge / …`) and CANCELLED runs are never verdicts.
- Stale-park recovery: a guest rung in `update_branch` clears a `validation_failed` park when the punished head is **decided** (≥1 real concluded check) and carries no red — the `real >= 1` guard preserves the fa#923 sticky-park semantics for undecided heads; machine parks keep gh-750 semantics untouched.
- AC3 observability: one dead-zone scan per tick (cached, probe failures fail closed) rides the factory-state snapshot via `deadZone` passthrough (`applyDeadZoneSnapshot`) and surfaces as `guest_prs_blocked_no_validation_path` in the tick summary.
- Layer order pinned in `smRuleLayers.js` + `test_smTickLayers.js` (`merge-validated` → `merge-validated-guest` → `fail-validation` → rework lanes — the #637/#682 invariants hold).

## How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestValidationPath.json   # 21 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json               # 718 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json                   # 5475 passed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Q[merge-validated-guest rule] -->|notMachine + armed + CLEAN + none/pending| G[guestZeroFailingMergeGate]
  G --> T[realCheckTally census]
  G --> E[isManualArm events probe]
  T -->|zero-failing + manual arm| M[merge_pr]
  T -->|red / in-flight / machine arm / no proof| R[refuse - fail closed]
  P[parked guest validation_failed] --> U[update_branch guest rung]
  U -->|decided head, no red| C[clear park + comment]
  U -->|undecided / red head| H[fa-923 park holds]
  B[blocked guests] --> DZ[deadZone snapshot] --> S[tick summary counter]
```

</details>

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

{"path":"outputs/response.md","content":"## What changed
Closes the guest-PR validation dead zone (live IstiN/flutter_agent_harness #1634/#1615/#1591: fork PRs sat `pr_approved` + CLEAN for hours with a manual `ai_validating` label — no merge, no validation). Adds a `merge-validated-guest` lane (deployed `sm_github.json`, ordered directly below `merge-validated`): human-authored (`notMachine`) armed+approved CLEAN guests whose rollup carries no concluded verdict may merge when the head's real check-run census is zero-failing and the `ai_validating` event was labeled by a non-machine actor.

## Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/guestValidationPath.js` (`realCheckTally`, `mergeableZeroFailing`, `recoverableZeroRed`, `isManualArm`, `newestArmEvent`, dead-zone carry) — all policy decisions unit-tested in isolation, loaded real by the smAgent tests.
- Merge gate `guestZeroFailingMergeGate` (rule flag `guestZeroFailing`) is fail-closed on every probe: real red, real in-flight check, any active head workflow run, missing/unreadable arm event, or probe error → refuse; bookkeeping stubs (`merge / …`) and CANCELLED runs are never verdicts.
- Stale-park recovery: a guest rung in `update_branch` clears a `validation_failed` park when the punished head is **decided** (≥1 real concluded check) and carries no red — the `real >= 1` guard preserves the fa#923 sticky-park semantics for undecided heads; machine parks keep gh-750 semantics untouched.
- AC3 observability: one dead-zone scan per tick (cached, probe failures fail closed) rides the factory-state snapshot via `deadZone` passthrough (`applyDeadZoneSnapshot`) and surfaces as `guest_prs_blocked_no_validation_path` in the tick summary.
- Layer order pinned in `smRuleLayers.js` + `test_smTickLayers.js` (`merge-validated` → `merge-validated-guest` → `fail-validation` → rework lanes — the #637/#682 invariants hold).

## How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestValidationPath.json   # 21 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json               # 718 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json                   # 5475 passed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  G --> T[realCheckTally census]
  G --> E[isManualArm events probe]
  T -->|zero-failing + manual arm| M[merge_pr]
  T -->|red / in-flight / machine arm / no proof| R[refuse - fail closed]
  P[parked guest validation_failed] --> U[update_branch guest rung]
  U -->|decided head, no red| C[clear park + comment]
  U -->|undecided / red head| H[fa-923 park holds]

```

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */

{"path":"outputs/response.md","content":"## What changed
Closes the guest-PR validation dead zone (live IstiN/flutter_agent_harness #1634/#1615/#1591: fork PRs sat `pr_approved` + CLEAN for hours with a manual `ai_validating` label — no merge, no validation). Adds a `merge-validated-guest` lane (deployed `sm_github.json`, ordered directly below `merge-validated`): human-authored (`notMachine`) armed+approved CLEAN guests whose rollup carries no concluded verdict may merge when the head's real check-run census is zero-failing and the `ai_validating` event was labeled by a non-machine actor.

## Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/guestValidationPath.js` (`realCheckTally`, `mergeableZeroFailing`, `recoverableZeroRed`, `isManualArm`, `newestArmEvent`, dead-zone carry) — all policy decisions unit-tested in isolation, loaded real by the smAgent tests.
- Merge gate `guestZeroFailingMergeGate` (rule flag `guestZeroFailing`) is fail-closed on every probe: real red, real in-flight check, any active head workflow run, missing/unreadable arm event, or probe error → refuse; bookkeeping stubs (`merge / …`) and CANCELLED runs are never verdicts.
- Stale-park recovery: a guest rung in `update_branch` clears a `validation_failed` park when the punished head is **decided** (≥1 real concluded check) and carries no red — the `real >= 1` guard preserves the fa#923 sticky-park semantics for undecided heads; machine parks keep gh-750 semantics untouched.
- AC3 observability: one dead-zone scan per tick (cached, probe failures fail closed) rides the factory-state snapshot via `deadZone` passthrough (`applyDeadZoneSnapshot`) and surfaces as `guest_prs_blocked_no_validation_path` in the tick summary.
- Layer order pinned in `smRuleLayers.js` + `test_smTickLayers.js` (`merge-validated` → `merge-validated-guest` → `fail-validation` → rework lanes — the #637/#682 invariants hold).

/**
 * Guest validation path (gh-113) — the pure half of the guest-PR
 * dead-zone fixes.
 *
 * Live shape (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-19, PRs #1634/#1615/#1591):
 * guest PRs from a fork sat APROVED + CLEAN + behind=0 for hours with a
 * MANUAL ai_validating label and never merged. Three facts compound:
 *
 *   1. The validation dispatch is fork-blind: `workflow_dispatch` with
 *      `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 on the base repo (gh-1075 fixed
 *      the AI-leg lane; the validate_pr lane stays branch-targeted), so
 *      no real validation run is ever dispatched on a guest head.
 *   2. The guest heads carry only the merge bot's SKIPPED stub checks
 *      ('merge / …'). The smProvider ROLLUP label deliberately reads
 *      'pending' for such a head (bookkeeping checks are "no verdict
 *      yet" — that label arms validate-fresh), so merge-validated
 *      (checks: green) never matches either.
 *   3. The red re-validation lane (rework-on-validation-failed) is
 *      machine-author-only, so a stale validation_failed park on a
 *      guest has no self-clear twin of gh-750.
 *
 * The owner-sanctioned policy this module implements: a MANUAL
 * ai_validating label on a guest PR is an EXTERNAL VALIDATION ARM —
 * the human vouches for the head — so the merge lane may treat a
 * zero-failing check rollup (no real red, no real in-flight check;
 * bookkeeping stubs and CANCELLED runs are not verdicts) as green for
 * guests, and the park ladder gains a guest rung that clears a stale
 * validation_failed when the punished head carries no red of its own.
 *
 * Exports:
 *   realCheckTally(checkRuns, bookeepingPrefixes) — the REAL check-run
 *       census { red, pending, real, bokept, canceled }. Deliberately
 *       NOT the smProvider rollup semantics: bookkeeping-only heads
 *       tally zero real checks here (the merge-side policy), while the
 *       rollup label reads 'pending' for them (the arming-side policy).
 *   mergeableZeroFailing(tally) — merge bar: red === 0 && pending === 0.
 *       A real in-flight check owns the verdict — never merge ahead of
 *       it. Degraded input (null) fails closed.
 *   recoverableZeroRed(tally) — park-recovery bar: red === 0 only. A
 *       real in-flight run is not red; its verdict re-parks a genuinely
 *       red head one cycle later. Degraded input fails closed.
 *   newestArmEvent(events) — the newest `labeled` event for
 *       ai_validating from an issue-events feed (chronological, so the
 *       LAST match wins); null when the feed carries none.
 *   isManualArm(armEvent, machineAuthor) — the external-arm test: the
 *       event exists and its actor is NOT a machine login (the gh-728
 *       comma-separated knob, gh-1025 [bot]-suffix normalization). No
 *       event → false (fail closed — an irreversible merge needs the
 *       proof). No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external
 *       (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all).
 *   blockedGuestEntry(item, pr, isGuest) — the dead-zone shape: guest +
 *       (pr_approved | ai_validating) + CLEAN + rollup none|pending.
 *       Returns the summary entry or null. A failed/absent status probe
 *       (pr === null) is NEVER counted (fail closed).
 *   mergeDeadZoneCary(prev, current) — the cross-tick carry for the
 *       factory-state snapshot: per-PR first-seen timestamps (age never
 *       resets while a guest stays blocked); guests that stopped being
 *       blocked drop out.
 *
 * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe
 * data. One hoisted require (./machineAuthor.js — a pure leaf), never
 * lazy (gh-823 pack-require rule).
 */
